title: Coarse scheme and algebraicity for abelian-level curve moduli
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $g\geq2$, and let $\ell\geq3$ be a prime invertible in $k$. Let $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ be the groupoid of smooth projective geometrically connected genus-$g$ curves with a full abelian level-$\ell$ structure, with objects and arrows exactly as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Then $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ is a separated Deligne--Mumford stack, smooth and of finite type over $k$, and it has a separated finite-type coarse moduli $k$-scheme $C_{g,\ell}$ with coarse morphism $c:\mathcal L_{g,\ell}\to C_{g,\ell}$. Coarse moduli, Deligne--Mumford stack and algebraic space have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: $c$ is initial among maps to algebraic spaces and induces a bijection of geometric isomorphism classes. Smoothness and finite type for the stack are tested on smooth scheme atlases, with quasi-compactness for finite type; the scheme morphism conventions are [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Section 2.3, paragraphs preceding Theorem 2.3.2, Theorem 2.3.2(1), and Section 2.3.3. Local PDF WANTED; primary author PDF read online.

proof.text: Write $\overline{\mathcal M}=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ and $\mathcal M=\mathcal M_{g,0}$. The unpointed stable coarse theorem supplies smoothness and the Deligne--Mumford property of $\overline{\mathcal M}$ and identifies $\mathcal M$ as an open substack. The stable-isomorphism theorem supplies finite type and finite diagonal, properties not inferred merely from the existence of a projective coarse scheme. Apply the open-substack part of the permanence lemma: $\mathcal M$ is smooth, separated, finite type and Deligne--Mumford, with finite diagonal.

Put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. For any $T\to\mathcal M$ corresponding to $f:X\to T$, projectivity in the specified projective-bundle convention makes $f$ proper by the projective-bundle-proper lemma. Apply the smooth-proper finite-cohomology local-system theorem to the constant rank-one $A$-module sheaf and $q=1$. Thus $\mathcal H=R^1f_*\underline A$ is locally constant with finite-dimensional fibres. The prime-coefficient proper-base-change theorem identifies $u^{-1}\mathcal H$ with $R^1(f_{T'})_*\underline A$ for every $u:T'\to T$, using the specified exchange map. No assumption that $T$ is Noetherian is used.

source.place: Tag 0GLI, proposition-loc-cst-torsion, with the proper-base-change theorem cited by the node

proof.text: On an etale cover of $T$ trivializing $\mathcal H$ as a finite $A$-module $B$, the frame sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_A(\underline{A^{2g}},\mathcal H)$ is the constant sheaf of the finite set $\operatorname{Isom}_A(A^{2g},B)$. That set may be empty, which still gives a finite locally constant sheaf. The finite-locally-constant representability theorem therefore gives a finite etale $T$-scheme $P_T$. To check the required functor on all $T$-schemes, use the proper-base-change identification in step 2 and inverse-image representability: pulling $P_T$ to $T'$ represents the pulled-back frame sheaf. Its sections over $T'$ are exactly the level structures on $X_{T'}$. An object of $T\times_{\mathcal M}\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ is $(Y,\lambda,\alpha:Y\simeq X_{T'})$; send it to $(\alpha^*)^{-1}\lambda$. Its inverse sends a frame $\mu$ to $(X_{T'},\mu,\mathrm{id})$. An arrow compatible with $\alpha$ is uniquely forced, so these functors are inverse up to the displayed isomorphism and the groupoid is discrete. This proves the finite-etale chart criterion for the forgetful map $p:\mathcal L_{g,\ell}\to\mathcal M$.

source.place: Tag 03RV (finite locally constant representability); explicit 2-fibre-product calculation with the moduli definition

proof.text: Apply the finite-etale-decoration part of the permanence lemma to the forgetful map from step 3 and the smooth finite-diagonal stack of step 1. It gives that $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ is a separated smooth finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack and that $p$ is representable finite etale. This proves all the stack assertions before any claim of scheme representability.

source.place: Finite-etale chart criterion and smooth/finite-type composition

proof.text: For a geometric object $(C,\lambda)$, an automorphism $a$ satisfies $a^*\lambda=\lambda$. Since $\lambda$ is an isomorphism, cancel it to obtain $a^*=\mathrm{id}$ on $H^1(C_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Geometric level faithfulness applies: the curve is smooth, projective, connected, of genus $g\geq2$, and $\ell\geq3$ is prime to the characteristic. Hence $a=\mathrm{id}$. Thus every geometric object of $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ has trivial automorphism group.

source.place: Section 2.3.3; geometric level faithfulness, no symplectic restriction

proof.text: Let $q:\overline{\mathcal M}\to Q_g$ be the coarse scheme provided by the stable coarse theorem. Apply coarse-open restriction to the open $\mathcal M\subset\overline{\mathcal M}$, using finite type and finite diagonal from the stable-isomorphism theorem. This gives an open subscheme $V\subset Q_g$ and a coarse morphism $\mathcal M\to V$. Apply inertia-free finite-cover coarse descent to $p:\mathcal L_{g,\ell}\to\mathcal M$: step 1 gives the finite-type Deligne--Mumford base with finite diagonal, step 3 gives representable finiteness, and step 5 gives trivial geometric automorphisms. Its conclusion represents $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ by a scheme $L$ finite over $V$. In particular this is a scheme, rather than only an algebraic space.

Take $C_{g,\ell}=L$ and let $c$ be the equivalence $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}\simeq h_L$ from step 6. For every algebraic space $Z$, composition with this equivalence identifies maps $L\to Z$ with maps $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}\to Z$; on every algebraically closed field it identifies the discrete set $L(\Omega)$ with geometric isomorphism classes. These are precisely the two coarse conditions. Since $L$ represents the stack, its identity atlas tests the smoothness and finite type proved in step 4, and its scheme diagonal is the diagonal of that stack. Thus $L$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, as required.

source.place: Coarse universal property; identity atlas of a scheme, with the moduli-groupoid conventions
